_comment: Edit with switchboard.py (add/remove/list), or by hand. Prices are USD per 1M tokens, in/out, recorded when the entry was added — they drift, so treat them as ordering, not billing. 'good_at' is fed verbatim to the router model when Auto picks.
_policy_note: Per-folder data policy and family tier, keyed on the working directory Claude Code reports in its own Environment block. Keys are path prefixes; the LONGEST match wins, so a subfolder inherits unless it names itself. data: 'claude' = Anthropic models only (nothing leaves the plan), 'zdr' = third party allowed but only routes with a zero-data-retention provider - this EXCLUDES vendor subscriptions like Kimi, which retain under the vendor's own terms rather than ours, 'any' = no restriction. 'any' is the default because it is what the router did before this existed; an unlisted folder keeps working exactly as it used to. tier: which variant a ~fam/ family row resolves to, default 'pro' - set 'flash' on a folder to take the cheap variant there. A request with no Environment block (a bare API client, not Claude Code) gets the default: the cwd cannot be known, and failing closed there would break every non-Claude-Code caller.

~/Documents/Vanguard._why: Highest security. Off-limits to Claude sessions by CLAUDE.md anyway; this is the wire-level backstop.

~/Documents/State Street._why: Finances. Third party is fine but it must not retain.

_providers_note: A vendor with its own Anthropic-compatible endpoint and its own subscription, matched on the first segment of the model id. path_prefix is joined to the incoming path, so /coding + /v1/messages -> /coding/v1/messages. The key file is read per request and never cached; your claude.ai token is stripped before the request leaves the machine. Set cache_control false if a vendor rejects the markers, and add to drop_fields anything it 400s on.
_upstreams_note: Display only — the router never reads this. Credential paths shown in the editor's PROVIDERS panel. Add rows here as more are wired up.

upstreams.name: anthropic
upstreams.label: Claude
upstreams.detail: credential forwarded untouched; never read, stored or logged here

upstreams.name: openrouter-nonzdr
upstreams.label: OpenRouter (no ZDR)
upstreams.note: metered; a workspace with no ZDR guardrail
upstreams.detail: Sent ONLY for models flagged zdr:false, which the folder policy must already permit. The guardrail lives on the workspace, not the request, so a second key in a permissive workspace is the only way to reach a non-ZDR provider. Rotate by overwriting the file.

kimi.label: Kimi
kimi.console_hint: This is the Kimi For Coding SUBSCRIPTION page. Do not use platform.moonshot.ai — that is the pay-as-you-go console, and its keys are the same shape but 401 against this endpoint.

oauth._auth_note: An OAuth bearer goes in Authorization, not x-api-key; login --oauth applies these to the provider on success.
oauth._headers_note: Measured 2026-09-04: auth.kimi.com accepts device_authorization and the token poll with NO vendor identity headers — identical responses with and without X-Msh-Platform/Version. So none are sent. Only genuine device info goes, and switchboard does not claim to be kimi_cli. If the backend ever starts requiring an identity, add it here and the disclosure fires again.

quota._note: The plan's own usage meters, polled by the router after each Kimi request and flattened into kimi-limits.json beside the log for the notch. Verified live 2026-09-15: answers usages.limit_5h / limit_month_total / limit_month_code, each {used_ratio, reset_time}; the same provider credential authenticates it. The lookalikes /coding/v1/usage, /coding/v1/quota and /coding/v1/users/me/quota are all 404. Responses carry no rate-limit headers, which is why this separate poll exists at all.

_picker_note: Gateway rows are published after the six built-in Claude rows. Order this list by how often each is picked by hand — Auto is always first. openrouter/auto is deliberately NOT listed: it is a delegation target for Auto (rule 4), not a hand-pick. Picking it directly can never select a subscription model, so every turn costs cash — the inverse of what Auto is for. Launch with --model openrouter/auto if it is ever wanted explicitly.
_lineup_note: Used by 'picker --apply': the WHOLE /model menu, in order, weighted by how likely each is to be picked by hand. Ten rows is the limit before Claude Code collapses the rest behind '… +N models'. A row with only a 'model' key fills its label and description from the catalog (blurb + price); give label/description explicitly for Claude ids, which are not catalog entries. Anything left out is still routable by Auto.

_failover_note: On 402/429/529 the router retries the next model here before answering. 401/403 is NOT included: a bad credential must never silently drain a different quota. A target containing '/' is METERED — failing over to one spends cash, so these are set deliberately, not by default.

models._tier_note: upstream_id/context are DISCOVERED, not assumed: `switchboard.py login` tries upstream_candidates best-first against the real key and writes whichever the plan actually serves. No official source states whether Kimi Code's 1M model is tier-gated, so do not trust a blog for it — re-run `login --check` after any plan change.

models.name: Kimi K3

models.name: OpenRouter Auto
models.good_at: ANY paid work with no specialist need. Delegates the choice: OpenRouter classifies the prompt into a task type and ranks models by community spend over 7 days, so it tracks the field without this catalog being maintained. Prefer it over naming a specific priced model unless that model has a SPECIALTY the task needs.

_arrow_note: The ←/→ row. Claude Code's effort slider reaches the wire as output_config.effort, and a row declared via ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION with SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES=effort,xhigh_effort,max_effort gets that slider even as a gateway id. So one picker row carries this shortlist and the arrows choose between them. Ordered weakest to strongest; an unmapped level falls to the strongest set.
